article_title: Kotlin 2.5.0 Reaches RC2, Adding a New Multiplatform Compilation Scheme and Fixing a Wasm Regression Found in RC

content_preview.title: Kotlin 2.5.0 Reaches RC2, Adding a New Multiplatform Compilation Scheme and Fixing a Wasm Regression Found in RC
content_preview.summary: Kotlin 2.5.0-RC2, published November 25, adds a new experimental Multiplatform compilation scheme and fixes a Wasm performance regression and Compose benchmark slowdown found in the Nov 11 RC.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

JetBrains has published Kotlin 2.5.0-RC2, a pre-release build that [kotlinlang.org's EAP page](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/eap.html) lists as released on November 25, 2026. The build follows [2.5.0-RC](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/tag/v2.5.0-RC), published November 11, which in turn followed [2.5.0-Beta2](/article/2026-10/26-kotlin-250-beta2-adds-experimental-companion-blocks-and-full-value-classes-a-kar-library-format-and-an-error-ahead-of-a-jdk-17-compiler-minimum)...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (535 words, within the 400-1200 range): Overview establishes provenance and chain of prior Herald coverage, a dedicated section separates genuinely new RC2 features from material already reported at Beta2, a 'Regressions caught and fixed in RC2' section gives specific issue IDs and verbatim titles, a release-timeline section quotes the vendor's own cadence language, and a 'What We Don't Know' section honestly scopes the article's limits (number of further RCs, exact December date, absence of independent third-party coverage) without overclaiming. Tone is flat and factual throughout; no editorializing.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 5 decompressed snapshots in sources/2026-11/kotlin-250-reaches-rc2-adding-a-new-multiplatform-compilation-scheme-and-fixing-a-wasm-regression-found-in-rc/ (source-0 through source-4, all status 200, manifest sha256 verified, suspicious_patterns null on every entry -- no injection attempt found). source-3 (kotlinlang.org/docs/eap.html): Build-details table confirms '2.5.0-RC2' 'Released: November 25, 2026' and the verbatim RC2-stage description 'Includes important fixes to finalize the release and confirm readiness' -- matches article exactly. source-1 (GitHub v2.5.0-RC2 release page): <relative-time datetime="2026-11-25T10:43:53Z"> confirms the Nov 25 date independently of kotlinlang; changelog text (stripped to plain text) confirms, in order, 'Backend. Wasm' category containing KT-91749 'Kotlin/Wasm: cos is ~47% slower in 2.5.0-RC than in 2.4.21' immediately followed by 'Compiler' category containing KT-91549 'Slowdown in compose benchmarks in Float.fromBits' -- the article's category attributions for both issues are correct. Also confirmed verbatim: KT-91488/KT-87563 under 'Tools. Compiler Plugins' (Lombok), KT-91414/KT-91591 under 'Tools. Compiler plugins. Compose', KT-90626/KT-90770 under 'Tools. Gradle. JS'. source-2 (GitHub v2.5.0-RC release page): <relative-time datetime="2026-11-11T10:19:34Z"> confirms the Nov 11 RC date; changelog confirms KT-84904 'Alpha release of Multi-Field Value Classes' and KT-90544 'Gradle, Multiplatform: Publication iteration misses JS, Wasm and Native targets since 2.5.0-Beta2 (after Kotlin Archive publishing changes)' verbatim. source-0 (kotlinlang.org/docs/whatsnew-eap.html): confirms the KMP compilation-scheme quote verbatim -- 'introduces a new experimental compilation scheme for Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) that makes the compiler handle common source sets more consistently with the IDE' and 'prevents common code from accidentally resolving to platform-specific declarations, improves consistency in overload resolution and type inference, and enables us to implement incremental compilation for common source sets' (article correctly substitutes 'us' with bracketed '[JetBrains]'); also confirms presence of Java 28, Swift export, es2020, .kar, companion blocks, full value classes and JDK 17 minimum as already-reported Beta2 carryover features. source-4 (kotlinlang.org/docs/releases.html): confirms verbatim 'Language releases (2.x.0) that bring major changes in the language and include tooling updates. Released once in 6 months' and the upcoming-schedule line '2.5.0: Planned for December 2026', described under the heading 'approximate schedule for upcoming stable Kotlin releases' -- matches the article's characterization that JetBrains has not committed to a specific December date. No claim in the article is unsupported by its cited source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked (two dates, seven issue IDs with their exact titles and categories, the KMP-scheme quote, the release-cadence quote, the December-2026 schedule line) traces verbatim to the snapshot text. The one slightly ambiguous sentence -- 'which in turn followed 2.5.0-Beta2, the Herald's previous coverage of this release cycle, published October 21' -- reads, by parallelism with the preceding RC clause ('published November 11'), as dating the Beta2 build's own release (October 21), not the Herald's article about it (which published October 26 per that article's frontmatter). This matches the prior article's own summary line ('Kotlin 2.5.0-Beta2, a pre-release published October 21'), so the claim is accurate on the correct reading, if a touch awkwardly phrased. Not a reportable error. Claim-accuracy audit (absence/quantifier/qualifier words) run against the raw submission text found only self-referential hedges in the 'What's new since Beta2' and 'What We Don't Know' sections (e.g. 'Independent third-party coverage or benchmarks of RC2 were not found among the sources reviewed for this article') -- these are honest scope disclaimers about the Herald's own research, not absolute claims about the world, and are correctly qualified. No hallucinated quotes, no fabricated specifics, no orphan source URLs (every body link is also in article.sources). Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article does not involve Anthropic, Claude, or any Anthropic-operated product as subject.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No promotional language, no unearned superlatives. The article explicitly notes an uncheckable claim ('The Herald has not built or run the release') and an inaccessible source ('that blog post returned an access error when the Herald tried to fetch it'), both appropriate transparency about the limits of the reporting.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. The Herald's only prior coverage of this release cycle is the October 26 Beta2 article (src/content/articles/2026-10/26-kotlin-250-beta2-...), which this article correctly references and distinguishes from (explicitly separating already-reported Beta2 features from genuinely new RC2 material). No other 2026-11 article covers Kotlin 2.5.0-RC/RC2; the only other November Kotlin-adjacent article is about Gradle's Kotlin DSL, an unrelated topic. Not a duplicate.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced release-tracking News piece. All five sources read and verified; every date, issue ID, issue title, category attribution, and quoted passage traces verbatim to the cited snapshot. No fabrications, no misattributions, no orphan sources, no suspicious patterns in any snapshot. Approved as submitted. Featured candidacy: 0 - routine incremental RC tracking of a known release cycle, useful to a defined Kotlin/KMP developer audience but not broadly significant.
